output.summary: A perennial herb hybrid occurring naturally in the Caucasus region, Russian comfrey grows on waste ground and disturbed soils. It has a deep taproot, hairy above-ground growth, and flowers that turn from pink to blue or remain purple.
output.edibilityNote: Documented for human consumption; Bocking No. 4 is recommended, but prolonged intake of its alkaloids may damage the liver, prompting food-use restrictions.
